It describes a crisis that started with a paper by somebody called Ioannidis published in PLoS Science in 2005. They found a mathematical way to predict how likely results of studies conducted in fields were real/true and found that in fields with small sample sizes, easy-to-come-by hypotheses and lots of latent constructs (like psychology), results are unlikely to be real/true. This led to lots of famous/classical studies being replicated in a big project, followed by "Many Labs 2 and 3", and they all had shocking results. Of the first big replication project, around 90-something % of the original studies had shown significant effects. Of the replicated studies, only 30 or 40-something % did. Of those, only under half the effects found were comparable to the originally found effects in effect size, the other effect sizes were about half as big. This led to a confidence crisis in psychology. So, summed up, the replication crisis means that studies can't be replicated/don't show significant effects/comparable effect sizes when replicated.
